item.title: Gen. Dan Caine reflects on responding to 9/11: "No doubt" nation was at war
item.description: Now the chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff, Gen. Dan Caine was a young fighter pilot mobilized in the response on Sept. 11, 2001.

item.title: Gen. Dan Caine describes taking to the skies in fighter jet to defend U.S. on 9/11
item.description: On Sept. 11, 2001, then-Maj. Dan Caine was chief of weapons and tactics for the 121st Fighter Squadron at Andrews Air Force Base in Maryland. Caine, now the chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff, tells Norah O'Donnell about jumping into action when the second plane hit the World Trade Center.

item.title: 3 generations of FDNY family share their tragic 9/11 story
item.description: Tony Dokoupil tells the story of a New York City Fire Department family that experienced 9/11 through three generations and how they remember the loved one they lost 25 years later.

item.title: Woman reunites with baby she saved on 9/11, now 25 years old
item.description: On Sept. 11, 2001, Darla Stuckey went to work at the New York Stock Exchange like any other morning. Then, moments after the World Trade Center attacks, she had a chance encounter that forever changed her life -- and that of a nine-month-old baby. Lesley Stahl has the story.

item.title: 25 years after 9/11: What America's longest war left behind
item.description: Imtiaz Tyab returned to Afghanistan, 25 years after 9/11, to report on what life is like there today, under Taliban rule.

item.title: 9/11 survivors, responders and families of victims reflect on 25 years since attacks
item.description: Friday marks 25 years since the Sept. 11, 2001, terrorist attacks that killed nearly 3,000 people. Survivors, responders and families of the victims spoke with CBS News about their memories of that day and its impact on their lives a quarter-century later.

item.title: Chicago rapper Lil Durk acquitted in Los Angeles murder-for-hire plot
item.description: A federal jury in Los Angeles has acquitted Grammy-winning Chicago rapper Lil Durk in a murder-for-hire plot targeting another rapper.

item.title: How a small New Jersey town recovered from loss after the 9/11 attacks
item.description: The small town of Summit, New Jersey, where several World Trade Center workers lived before 9/11, lost a number of community members in the attacks. 60 Minutes correspondent Leslie Stahl reports.

item.title: Previewing championship weekend at the U.S. Open
item.description: Nine-time doubles Grand Slam winner Bethanie Mattek-Sands joins CBS News to break down this weekend's grand finale to the U.S. Open tennis tournament.

item.title: Recapping the Republicans' midterm convention
item.description: Republicans held their first ever midterm convention this week with President Trump and Vice President JD Vance delivering remarks. CBS News' Zak Hudak has a recap.

item.title: Inside Afghanistan under Taliban rule, 25 years after 9/11
item.description: CBS News' Imtiaz Tyab reports from Kabul, Afghanistan, on what life is like there 25 years after 9/11.

item.title: Heroes of Flight 93 remembered for their courage 25 years on from 9/11
item.description: On Sept. 11, 2001, the passengers and crew bravely decided to storm the cockpit of United Airlines Flight 93, preventing the terrorists who had taken control of the plane from flying it to Washington, D.C.

item.title: CIA declassifies dozens of never-before-seen 9/11 documents
item.description: The CIA released 71 reports from the months and years leading up to 9/11, providing a new look at what the spy agency told two presidents before the deadly strikes.

item.title: Man arrested in death of Tasia Fortune, woman found hanging from tree
item.description: Mississippi police have arrested a man in the death of Tasia Fortune, a Black woman found hanging from a tree last month.

item.title: 25 years after 9/11 attacks, America reflects and remembers
item.description: Four former presidents were at the World Trade Center memorial site for 9/11 commemorations, while President Trump spoke at the Pentagon.

item.title: Diesel hits record $6 a gallon as Iran-backed Houthis take key Red Sea territory
item.description: The moves by the Houthis make it easier for the Iran-backed rebels to target ships transiting the crucial Bab el-Mandeb Strait for Saudi Arabian oil exports.

item.title: Details on U.S. import bans against Canadian alcohol, other goods
item.description: President Trump has announced a ban against the import of some Canadian products, including most Canadian alcohol, some dairy products and motorcycles. CBS News' Megan Cerullo has more.

item.title: State of al‑Qaeda 25 years after 9/11 attacks
item.description: 25 years after 9/11, we rarely hear about the state of the organization responsible for the attacks. The Atlantic recently put out a piece on al-Qaeda that says in part, "analysts can't decide if the terrorist organization is all but defunct or more threatening than ever." The article's author, Graeme Wood, joins "The Takeout" to discuss.

item.title: Steve Hartman returns to Shanksville, 25 years after covering the crash of Flight 93 on 9/11
item.description: Steve Hartman takes us on the road to visit the site of the 9/11 United Flight 93 crash in Shanksville, Pennsylvania.

item.title: Custodian who saved several people, escaped World Trade Center's North Tower remembers 9/11
item.description: World Trade Center custodian William Rodriguez had planned on taking the day off on September 11, 2001. His boss begged him to come in, and later that day he would become one of the last known people to leave the North Tower alive. Rodriguez joins CBS News to share his story.

item.title: David Martin remembers reporting from the Pentagon on 9/11
item.description: CBS News' David Martin was at the Pentagon on the morning of September 11, 2001. He shares his recollections from that day.

item.title: Heightened security in Ireland as Trump set to visit, attend Irish Open at his golf club
item.description: President Trump is set to fly to Dublin, Ireland, for a state visit this weekend, before attending the Irish Open golf tournament at his golf club in Doonbeg. Nancy Cordes has more.

item.title: USS George Washington, warship deployed to NYC after 9/11, is now involved in Iran war
item.description: Tom Hanson lands on the USS George Washington, a ship that patrolled the waters near New York City after 9/11, which is now located near the Strait of Hormuz in the fight against Iran.

item.title: Trump admin. to send $500 checks to nearly 1 million ACA enrollees
item.description: Affordable Care Act recipients in 30 states are set to receive the $500 checks starting in October. Here's why.

item.title: Ex-CIA official found with $40 million in gold bars in plea deal talks
item.description: The court filing did not indicate what charges David Rush could plead to.

item.title: 9/11: The Takeout with Major Garrett
item.description: Ceremonies held to mark quarter-century since 9/11 attacks; a look at the numbers 53 days away from the November midterm elections.

item.title: How lower-paid workers are getting their biggest pay raise in years
item.description: Some workers are seeing stronger wage growth by switching jobs, while others are "job-hugging" because of AI, research shows.

item.title: Suspects in $6 million romance scam targeting women extradited to U.S.
item.description: The men, who were arrested in the South African city of Cape Town in 2021, are set to be handed over to officials from the FBI.

item.title: Record-setting cyclospora outbreak is over, U.S. health officials say
item.description: The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention said there is no longer a risk of people getting sick with cyclosporiasis from this outbreak and is confident that all related iceberg lettuce is off the market.

item.title: CPI rose at 3.4% pace in August, raising odds of Fed rate hike this month
item.description: The report comes at a pivotal moment for the Federal Reserve, which is scheduled to meet next week to decide whether to hike interest rates.
